When the notes come from Washington it is the government that answers them, and the Supreme Command has learned since the summer that it is told what it may do. The army asks for nothing in its own name. The ministers who sign are the ministers who have governed since 1917. A request that comes from a government with its own standing is a different thing from one that comes from a headquarters, and the account that later put the blame on the civilians would have been harder to tell. What actually happened: Bethmann Hollweg was forced out in July 1917, in the crisis over the Reichstag's peace resolution, at the insistence of the Supreme Command, and the governments that followed were weaker. Prince Max of Baden became Chancellor on 3 October 1918 and the request to President Wilson went out in the first days of that month. The armistice was signed on 11 November, and within a year the account of an army betrayed at home was in print.Your commandColonel62 out of 100Groun
